summary: Per-tool schema-prefetch handshake adds 60-200ms per tool call, causing multi-tool sequences to time out
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports multi-step tool call workflows intermittently exceed end-to-end timeouts. Root cause suspected to be a synchronous schema-prefetch/handshake for every tool invocation introduced in SDK v2.7.
Impact: Several long-running customer workflows with 3+ sequential tool calls see 30-80% increase in tail latency; some requests hit application-level timeouts (30s) and fail. This affects customer-facing production traffic for ScribeAI (dedicated pool).
Environment: Production (us-east), dedicated capacity, SDK v2.7.1 pinned. Behavior not reproducible on staging because of different traffic multiplexing and disabled schema-prefetch flag there.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy ScribeAI workload against Redwood prod endpoint (prod, us-east) with SDK v2.7.1 and tool-call flow enabled.
2) Issue a request that triggers a chain of 4 tool calls (e.g., parse -> enrich -> db_write -> notify) with streaming disabled.
3) Observe end-to-end latency per request in customer logs and in Redwood Console route-level dashboard.
4) Compare traces: look for a ~60-200ms synchronous round trip per tool call with tag 'schema-prefetch' or 'validator-ping'.
logs: 2026-03-12T14:22:10.004Z api-gateway[req-7f1c]: request closed by client after 30s timeout (reqId=def456)
Note: traces show a near-linear increase ~130ms per tool call for affected traces.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: correlated customer error spikes with SDK v2.7.1 rollout on 2026-03-10; no infra changes in Dedicated pool around that time.
SRE (Elena) ran p99 latency queries on route: toolcall-heavy routes show +120ms p99 delta vs baseline for consecutive days.

Tracing indicates a synchronous HTTP gRPC call from function-proxy to schema-validator for every tool invocation; the validator is configured in SDK to 'prefetch' schemas when tool metadata flags are present.
Hypothesis: schema-prefetch handshake was added to improve validation correctness but was implemented synchronously on the hot path without caching across a request lifecycle.
Reproduction: Disabling SDK prefetch flag at client side reduces per-tool hop by ~110-140ms in controlled test (ScribeAI test harness).
Risk: Disabling prefetch may re-expose certain schema mismatch errors; need to ensure validation is performed asynchronously or cached per-request.
Related internal ticket INT-4031 raised to look at schema-validator scaling and potential batching options.
Observed no excess CPU/GPU saturation; validator latency appears to be the add-on hop (not serving runtime token generation).
Customer reports workflows with streaming off are worst affected because SDK waits for handshake before issuing next call.
comments: Support - Aisha: Logged after customer report. Attached sample traces and asked ScribeAI for a minimal repro payload.
ScribeAI - Daniel (engineer): Provided two failing request IDs and a local repro using SDK v2.7.1. Noted failure rate ~6% during business hours.
SRE - Elena: Confirmed p99 increase; created INT-4031 to investigate validator behavior and whether batching could help.
Eng - Marco: Investigating SDK change that added 'schema-prefetch' handshake. Drafting quick mitigation to short-circuit handshake when a cached schema exists.
Support - Aisha: Proposed temporary client-side workaround (set REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH=false) and asked eng to validate implications.
ScribeAI - Daniel: Applied client-side workaround on a small percentage of traffic and observed significant drop in timeouts (from 4.2% to 0.5%).
resolution: Mitigated and rolling fix. Temporary mitigation: customer set REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH=false which removed synchronous handshake and reduced timeouts. Engineering pushed SDK patch v2.7.2 that makes prefetch asynchronous and adds per-request schema cache; serving-runtime PR added a short-circuit for cached schemas.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Temporary mitigation validated by customer (client-side flag) — immediate reduction in timeouts observed.
2026-03-13: SDK v2.7.2 released (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/987) — makes schema-prefetch async and adds per-request LRU cache (TTL 2m).
2026-03-13: Serving-runtime PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2314) added tracing tags and a bypass when schema present in cache to avoid validator round-trip.
Follow-up: INT-4031 assigned to Validator team to evaluate persistent caching, batching validations for high-tool-count requests, and a longer-term TTL/consistency plan.
Customer follow-up: ScribeAI confirmed they will roll SDK v2.7.2 to 100% in 48 hours and requested a post-deploy verification window for latency regressions.
Postmortem/Action: Create Confluence postmortem and update SDK release notes indicating change in default behavior and guidance for customers on schema-heavy flows.
